conditions.host: 6 vCPU AMD EPYC 3251, 5.2 GiB RAM, Linux 7.0.0-42
conditions.toolchain: Go 1.27.3, GCC 15.2.0; native SQLite 3.53.4 via mattn/go-sqlite3 v1.14.52
conditions.caveat: Shared development VM; timings are observations, not service-level objectives. The commit probe compares a diagnostic NORMAL mode with the shipped FULL policy.

large_book.fixture: 250,000 posted postings over 3,020 accounts, two currencies, five years
large_book.note: Script max RSS includes benchmark compilation/execution; the test-only run previously peaked near 301 MiB.

sqlite_commit_probe.description: Isolated native SQLite WAL commit probe; 500 transactions with TEXT values, two balanced postings and one audit row. Includes preparation, writes and commit. Separate upstream driver connection permits diagnostic NORMAL comparison; shipped app always uses FULL. Not a complete application workflow or production latency guarantee.

deployment_probe.binary_source: da2563b4; later main commits only patch frontend dependencies, so the served Go runtime shape is unchanged

reproduction.schema: open the migrated database with Python sqlite3 and query sqlite_master, pragma page_size/page_count, and os.path.getsize
reproduction.deployment: start dist/rekenraam serve with APP_ENV=development, a temporary DATABASE_URL and HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1:16999; poll /healthz; read VmRSS from /proc/PID/status; stop with SIGTERM

limitations: No live PostgreSQL/MySQL benchmark was run: that would require porting the full schema and repository workload, and a generic pgbench number would not be comparable.
The commit probe uses a tiny synthetic schema, not the application transaction path or the production schema.
The deployment startup probe used a development build; release candidate startup/signing evidence remains separate.
Shared-host storage and CPU variance affect commit and large-book timings.
